key_headlines.summary: South Korea posted a record-high February current account surplus of approximately 35 trillion won, driven by semiconductor exports which extended their 34-month consecutive surplus streak, the second-longest run since the 2000s.

key_headlines.title: KOSPI Rebounds 7% on Geopolitical Relief as Market Risk Sentiment Improves
key_headlines.summary: The KOSPI index surged nearly 7% to 5,872.34 on relief from the US-Iran ceasefire agreement, recovering above the 5,800 level for the first time since late March, while the won-dollar exchange rate fell below 1,500 won.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's economy showed mixed signals as geopolitical tensions momentarily eased with the US-Iran ceasefire agreement. Prime Minister Kim Min-seok convened an emergency economic meeting to address sustainability transitions and packaging material supply chain stabilization. The ceasefire prompted immediate relief across financial markets, with crude oil prices dropping 20% and the won strengthening significantly. However, underlying uncertainties persist regarding the durability of the ceasefire and its long-term impact on energy security. The government is actively monitoring Strait of Hormuz passage normalization and preparing contingency measures.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: South Korea's fiscal position improved in January-February with the national deficit reaching 14 trillion won, a 3.9 trillion won improvement year-over-year despite increased national debt of 44.3 trillion won over two months. Tax revenues increased substantially, with income tax, value-added tax, and securities transaction tax all rising together, driven by growing employment and economic activity. The Korea Development Institute warned that geopolitical risks from the Middle East conflict pose downside risks to growth, though exports and domestic demand showed gradual improvement. Foreign investor capital outflows from government bonds totaled 7 trillion won in March due to external uncertainties, causing increased volatility in the bond market.
sections.Financial Markets: South Korean financial markets experienced significant volatility, with the KOSPI falling at the open on April 9 but recovering to close 5,872.34 the previous day, up 6.87% on ceasefire relief. The won-dollar exchange rate strengthened from 1,480 won levels, breaking below 1,500 won for the first time in ten trading days as market risk sentiment improved dramatically. The KOSDAQ index also posted gains of 5.12%, closing at 1,089.85, reflecting broad market relief from geopolitical tensions. Foreign investors turned net sellers while institutions and individuals became net buyers, indicating shifting portfolio positioning amid reduced uncertainty.
sections.Industry & Technology: South Korea's battery industry faced mounting pressure as global electric vehicle battery market (excluding China) grew 12.1% in January-February, but Korean battery makers' market share fell by 8.8 percentage points due to Chinese competitors CATL and BYD expanding dominance. M-Plus reported breakthrough developments in solid-state battery production technology, resolving key bottlenecks in manufacturing and electrode production that could enable next-generation applications in energy storage systems, robotics, and electric vehicles. The solid-state battery market represents a critical opportunity for Korean manufacturers to regain competitiveness against Chinese rivals. Industry experts view the technology as essential for future energy and mobility solutions.
sections.Real Estate: April apartment sales outlook index dropped sharply to 60.9, down 35.4 points month-over-month and reaching the lowest level since January 2023, as geopolitical concerns and lending restrictions hit the real estate market. Seoul's outer district apartment markets saw record-high transaction prices as renters unable to find jeonse (deposit lease) properties flowed into the purchase market, with some single-unit apartments jumping 100 million won in value. A seven-person household with perfect credit score (84 points) won lottery draw for Acro de Seocho redevelopment project, requiring 15+ years of homelessness tenure. Kangwon province's Reneoceam Goseong First View apartment complex opened its model house on April 10, offering 263 units ranging from 74 to 183 square meters.
sections.International Economy: The US-Iran ceasefire agreement triggered immediate relief in global markets, though underlying tensions remain as Israeli airstrikes on Lebanon on the first day of ceasefire killed over 1,000 people, prompting Iran to suggest potential agreement violations. Trump announced plans to collaborate with Iran on removing deeply buried nuclear residue and threatened 50% tariffs on any nation selling weapons to Iran, signaling conditions tied to the ceasefire. The US Senate continues debating Federal Reserve Chair nominee Warsh amid Republican party divisions, with implications for future monetary policy decisions beyond the current two-week ceasefire window. Global equities rebounded sharply on ceasefire hopes, though investors await concrete progress in scheduled peace negotiations beginning April 11 in Islamabad.
sections.AI & Economy: South Korean private equity funds (PEFs) increasingly invest in artificial intelligence companies, shifting from traditional venture capital into growth-stage AI enterprises expecting rapid returns and strong market tailwinds. Goldman Sachs research indicates that AI-driven labor displacement could raise unemployment by up to 0.5 percentage points over the next decade, with displaced workers facing 10% wage reductions upon reemployment in other sectors. Optical communication infrastructure stocks gained prominence as AI data center competition shifts focus from chip performance to data transfer efficiency, attracting AI infrastructure investment beyond semiconductors and power sectors into networking and optical telecommunications. South Korea's 30-year CDMA mobile technology heritage generated 125 trillion won in production effects and 1.42 million jobs, positioning the nation to leverage legacy expertise for next-generation AI infrastructure development.
sections.Others: Suspicious trading patterns emerged as 1.4 trillion won in crude oil futures were sold massively three hours before Trump's ceasefire announcement, followed by a 15% price collapse, raising insider trading concerns similar to patterns preceding the previous month's attack postponement. GS Construction announced a strategic partnership with Hana Financial Group for expanded investment in advanced strategic industries, particularly data center and digital infrastructure projects through investment funds and project financing arrangements. The US State Department announced first peace negotiations scheduled for April 11 in Islamabad, with Vice President JD Vance, Middle East envoy Steve Witkoff, and son-in-law Jared Kushner leading the American delegation to pursue permanent settlement terms.
